newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Albright says Yeltsin "completely in control".
newsitem.headline: Albright says Yeltsin "completely in control".

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Friday after talks with Boris Yeltsin that the Russian president was "in charge" and actively engaged in discussions on NATO enlargement.

"He was...very much in charge...very engaged," Albright told reporters after a one-hour meeting with Yeltsin at the Kremlin. "He was very sharp in terms of what he wanted to achieve... I would say he is completely in control."

Albright, on her first overseas trip since becoming America's top diplomat last month, was the first U.S. official to meet Yeltsin since he had heart surgery last November and fell ill with pneumonia in January.

She said she had given him a letter from President Bill Clinton in which the American leader looked forward to a planned summit in Helsinki next month and discussed what they want to achieve there, Albright's spokesman said.

Most reporters present as Yeltsin greeted Albright in his ornate green and white oval meeting room said the Russian president looked painfully thin, waxen and heavily made-up. He walked steadily, but his voice seemed weaker than in the past.

U.S. officials said Albright, who is fluent in Russian, spoke Russian at the start and end of the meeting, dispensing with the interpreters' services from Russian to English in the final third of the meeting because she understood and the leaders wanted to speed up the talks.
